data.title: To Help Lower Prices, Trump Removes Tariffs on Ground Beef Imports
data.description:
To help lower prices for consumers, U.S. President Donald Trump is allowing up to 300,000 metric tons of ground beef to be imported into America over the next three months free of tariffs. Trump said, "We have a commitment that this beef will be sold at 25% below current market prices." However, Trump did not say which companies had made commitments to sell ground beef at a discount.

The National Cattlemen's Beef Association, a lobby group, criticized the move, saying it would not address Trump's stated intention of helping consumers or lead to another claim Trump made that removing tariffs would increase the size of the U.S. beef herd. Beef imports into the U.S. currently face an average tariff of 26.4%.

Cattle Herds and Beef Prices

Beef prices in the U.S have soared this year as America's cattle herd steadily declines due to years of drought and high feed costs. Recent data from the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics shows that lean ground beef averaged $8.41 per pound in July of this year, while beef steaks averaged $12.00 to $13.50 per pound depending on the cut of meat.

According to the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA), the U.S. cattle herd now stands at its smallest size since the 1950s, when America's population was half its size today. The number of cattle slaughtered in the U.S. has declined to 2.2 million this year, down from 2.5 million a year ago. Beef production in America has fallen by 300,000 pounds to 1.9 million over the same time frame, pushing prices higher.

data.title: Uber Stock Rises Despite $966 Million Fine from Dutch Regulators
data.description:
Shares of Uber (UBER) are rising today even though the ride-hailing company faces an €825 million ($966 million) fine. This comes after the Dutch Data Protection Authority ruled that Uber improperly used automated systems to suspend some drivers by not providing enough human review and by failing to properly explain some decisions. According to Reuters, the penalty would be the second-largest ever issued under Europe's GDPR privacy rules. Uber strongly disagrees with the decision and plans to appeal.

Interestingly, the case covers incidents between 2020 and 2022. During that period, Uber's systems sometimes suspended drivers after detecting possible fraud. For example, the system could flag a driver if it believed the driver took unnecessary detours to increase a fare. It could also flag someone who accepted trips without intending to complete them.

The problem is that European privacy law places limits on major decisions made entirely by computer systems. If an automated decision can seriously affect someone's life or job, regulators generally require meaningful human review. People must also have a way to challenge the decision. Dutch regulators concluded that Uber did not meet those requirements in some cases.

Unsurprisingly, Uber disputes that finding. The company says that temporary suspensions were generally short. It also says that permanent fraud-related account removals required human review. Uber added that its current policies allow drivers to dispute suspensions. In addition, since Uber plans to appeal, the $966 million headline number may not end up being the company's final cost.

Why the Size of the Fine Stands Out

Nevertheless, Uber argues that the penalty is far too large compared with the number of drivers affected. The company says that only 126 European drivers were deactivated because of low customer ratings in 2021. Uber also denies that permanent deactivations were ever fully automated. The size of the penalty also stands out historically because only Meta Platforms' (META) €1.2 billion GDPR fine from 2023 has been larger. Meta is appealing that decision as well.

Still, major European fines against U.S. technology companies can take years in court, and some have eventually been reduced or overturned. Therefore, investors should not automatically assume Uber will ultimately pay the full amount.

data.title: U.S. Military Says It Helped Move 660 Million Barrels of Oil Through Strait of Hormuz
data.description:
The U.S. military says it has helped tankers transport more than 660 million barrels of crude oil through the Strait of Hormuz waterway near Iran since May of this year. U.S. Central Command says the U.S. military assisted 1,300 commercial vessels transit the Strait of Hormuz in recent months. This suggests more than seven million barrels of oil per day has shipped through the Strait in the past three weeks.

The shipments claimed by the U.S. military are larger than private sector estimates but still less than half the 20 million barrels per day of crude oil that passed through the Strait of Hormuz prior to the Iran war erupting earlier this year. Still, the U.S. military says that a substantial amount of crude oil is passing through the Strait of Hormuz despite Iran's ongoing attacks on ships in the waterway.

Conflicting Accounts

Exactly how much oil is coming out of Strait of Hormuz each day remains unclear. Both the U.S. and Iranian governments continue to provide conflicting and changing estimates that are usually much higher or lower than data from independent shipping companies and commodities tracking firms. The Trump administration recently claimed that 10 million barrels a day exited the Strait in recent weeks.

Maritime intelligence firm Windward estimates that crude oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz averaged about five million barrels a day in July, four million barrels per day in June, and only 1.6 million barrels a day in May of this year. The Trump administration recently abandoned military action in Iran and has moved instead to applying economic sanctions on the country.

Brent crude oil, the international standard, is trading at just under $94 a barrel on Aug. 21, having risen more than 5% in the past week.

data.title: Nvidia Stock Valuation: Is NVDA Cheap or Expensive Before Q2 Earnings?
data.description:
Nvidia (NVDA) is heading into its fiscal Q2 earnings on August 26 with a high bar to clear. Nvidia stock trades at a forward GAAP P/E of 23.17, below the sector average of 30.06. That suggests NVDA is not as expensive as some peers based on expected earnings. The upcoming earnings report could test whether that lower valuation is justified.

Interestingly, Nvidia is not cheap based on past earnings, but its strong profit growth makes its forward valuation more reasonable. A strong outlook could push NVDA to new highs, while weaker margins or delays in Blackwell shipments could weigh on the stock. For retail investors, full-year revenue guidance may matter more than the headline earnings beat.

What Experts Say About Nvidia's Valuation

Some experts see Nvidia as undervalued despite its strong AI growth and premium position in the chip market. EMJ Capital Founder and President Eric Jackson said Nvidia stock has been "cheap for a while." He noted that smaller AI chip players such as Marvell (MRVL) can trade at higher multiples because they are smaller and investors expect faster growth from them.

Morningstar also sees value in Nvidia. The firm said investors have shifted toward other AI semiconductor plays, including memory and optical chip stocks. Still, it sees upside for Nvidia if the company stays on track to meet its near- and medium-term revenue targets.

Meanwhile, Bank of America's analyst Vivek Arya is even more bullish on the valuation. His sum-of-the-parts analysis suggests Nvidia's free cash flow could be valued 34% to 50% higher than the current stock price, even after factoring in financing risks. He said investors may be overstating those risks, creating a "compelling opportunity."

Arya expects Nvidia to provide more details on its off-balance-sheet commitments when it reports earnings on August 26. Earlier this week, he reiterated his Buy rating and $350 price target on NVDA stock.

What Analysts Expect From Nvidia's Q2 Earnings

Heading into earnings, Wall Street remains highly bullish on NVDA, with 32 out of 33 analysts giving the stock a Buy rating. Analysts expect EPS of $2.09, nearly double the $1.05 reported a year ago. Revenue is forecast to jump 95% year-over-year to $92.04 billion.

data.title: OpenAI Is Closing in Fast on Anthropic With U.S. Businesses, Ramp Data Shows
data.description:
New data shows OpenAI, the creator of ChatGPT, catching up with Anthropic, the AI firm behind Claude, among U.S. businesses on Ramp, a renowned fintech company. The data, covering more than 70,000 U.S. businesses that use Ramp for corporate spend management, shows Anthropic's market share peaked at nearly 44% in July, while OpenAI held roughly 40%. Notably, the latest shift comes after Anthropic overtook OpenAI in business adoption three months ago.

OpenAI Narrows Anthropic's Lead Business AI Adoption, Ramp Says

In an August 20 X post, Ramp lead economist Ara Kharazian said OpenAI is gaining ground with its U.S. business users in the third quarter, while Anthropic's lead has narrowed. The data comes from Ramp's AI Index, which tracks AI use and spending across more than 70,000 U.S. businesses that use its bill pay and corporate card products.

According to Ramp, Anthropic first took the lead in May, when it reached 41% of Ramp's paying business users, compared with 39% for OpenAI. By July, Anthropic had extended that lead by 43.5% of businesses in the index paid for subscriptions or tokens. However, recent data show that OpenAI is now growing faster in Q3 to date. 

In the same July, OpenAI's share rose by 0.23%, narrowing the gap by about 0.87%. While these figures do not yet show OpenAI overtaking Anthropic, it highlights how close the ChatGPT creator is to reclaiming the ground it lost. Meanwhile, Ramp said the trend could still change before the quarter ends.

GPT-5.6 Sol Helps OpenAI Gain Ground as AI Demand Grows

OpenAI's recent growth suggests that businesses are now showing more interest in AI providers as new models become available. Kharazian attributed part of OpenAI's growth to its latest AI model family, GPT-5.6 Sol. 

The economist said the model is becoming an increasingly popular choice among developers. He also said Anthropic's Fable 5 model has seen weaker adoption because of its higher cost and data retention needs.

At the same time, overall demand for paid AI services continues to grow among Ramp customers. Data from Ramp show that the share of businesses paying for AI services rose from 50% in March to nearly 56% in July. 

The increase in AI adoption gives both OpenAI and Anthropic room to grow their revenue, even as they compete for a larger share of corporate spending.

OpenAI and Anthropic remain private companies, meaning only accredited investors can buy their shares before a potential IPO. data.title: U.S. Treasury Secretary Hints at Bigger Bond Repurchases as Yields Continue to Rise
data.description:
U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has said that buybacks of government bonds could accelerate as yields on both the long- and short-dated notes continue to rise. Specifically, Bessent said that the U.S. Treasury's buyback program of government debt could surpass the $4 billion announced earlier this week.

"We are going to make a market in these. We routinely do buybacks, and we're going to increase the size of the buyback… It could be more than $4 billion per issue," said Bessent, speaking to the media. The comments from Bessent come as yields on U.S. Treasurys continue to rise, with the yield on the benchmark 10-year government bond up 0.026 percentage points to 4.724% on Aug. 21.

The current yield on the 30-year U.S. Treasury is 5.25%. However, it hit a multi-year high of 5.30% earlier in the week amid growing concerns among investors.

What's Pushing Treasury Yields Higher

"We have a big toolkit," Bessent added when speaking to the media. "Part of it is signaling here to show that we believe yields don't reflect the underlying fundamentals of this Iran conflict. We will get on the other side of this."

The U.S. Treasury announced on Aug. 19 that it planned to intervene in the bond market to lower rising yields that have exerted downward pressure on stocks. Bessent initially said the Treasury would "at least double" the amount of 10-year, 20-year, and 30-year Treasury bonds it buys back from $2 billion to $4 billion. The increased buybacks are to start on Sept. 9 and remain effective through Nov. 4 of this year.

Despite the increased government buybacks, Treasury yields continue to trend higher due to several factors. These include concerns about the Iran war, rising crude oil prices, and persistent inflation in the U.S. economy. Growing concerns about U.S. debt levels are also impacting the bond market after America's national debt reached a record $40 trillion earlier this week, shaking investor confidence.

data.title: SpaceX Stock Falls Below $135 after Second Unlock — What Comes Next?
data.description:
SpaceX (SPCX) stock fell 2% at Friday's market open, after dropping 4.1% on Thursday. The stock slipped below its $135 IPO price as about 319 million shares became eligible for trading. Trading volume also jumped above normal levels, suggesting the latest unlock added pressure to the stock.

SPCX Share Unlock: Why the Stock Fell

Yesterday's unlock came just weeks after an even larger 912 million-share unlock on August 6, 2026. Together, more than 1.2 billion shares have now entered the tradable float in a short period. That has sharply increased the supply of shares available to investors and roughly doubled the tradable float.

SpaceX has a set lockup plan for shares held by staff, early backers and other pre-IPO holders. So, the shares are coming to market in waves, not all at once. More early holders can now sell their shares. The added supply has also led to higher-than-usual trading volume, even as SpaceX has kept up strong growth.

Other Factors Impacting SPCX Stock

SpaceX is reportedly interested in Grain Management's $6 billion spectrum portfolio, which could support its satellite-to-phone service. AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) is also said to be eyeing the same licenses. The licenses became available after Grain completed a spectrum swap with T-Mobile (TMUS) earlier this month.

Meanwhile, Anthropic is reportedly targeting an IPO by the end of 2026 that could match or top SpaceX's record $86 billion IPO valuation. Bloomberg reports that Anthropic could file for an IPO as soon as the end of August. The comparison keeps SPCX stock in focus.

What Comes Next?

The next big tests for SPCX stock will come as more shares become available. Two more releases are expected in October, with each freeing about 328 million shares. An even bigger test could come after SpaceX reports its Q3 results in November. That would put much more new supply on the market than the recent August unlocks.

More shares could then unlock as the main post-IPO lock-up period ends in December. Meanwhile, Elon Musk's 6.42 billion shares remain locked until June 2027.

For investors, SPCX stock could see more price swings around each unlock date as more shares become available. The company will need continued business growth to offset the added share supply. Strong earnings, Starlink growth, and progress on Starship could help investors absorb the new shares.
